body: Two measurement problems. First, FR-012/US-3 propose a Wilcoxon signed-rank test on paired predicted probabilities to judge whether the integrated model improves over the baseline. Paired probabilities do not measure performance: two models can assign nearly identical probabilities yet differ in accuracy, or differ wildly in probabilities while being equally accurate. The standard of evidence here should be a paired test on per-isolate correctness or loss (e.g., McNemar on classification outcomes, or a bootstrap/DeLong comparison of AUCs on the outer test set). As written, the significance test does not establish the claim it is asked to support. Second, FR-020 fixes the required sample at ~1,400 isolates per task for effect size 0.1, while the project plan limits the total dataset to ~1,000 isolates split across two species and six antibiotics. By the spec's own power criterion, essentially every species-antibiotic task will be flagged under-powered before training begins, and FR-014 then forbids proceeding. The power requirement and the data budget are mutually inconsistent; either the effect size target or the isolate limit must be reconciled, or the spec should state plainly that the study is powered only for larger effects.
